resources.string: Look up domain or public IP registration information.
User-initiated external lookup. Results stay in memory; no lookup History is saved.

This query contacts the IANA-selected registration service. It can see the displayed domain or public IP, your connection IP and request metadata. A directory refresh also contacts IANA. No LAN inventory or diagnosis History is sent. Results stay in memory.
Resolving and checking the service endpoint

HTTPS uses the active system network and its configured proxy route. TLS verifies the original service hostname, not a proxy or mapped IP.
No object was returned for this query. This does not establish availability or ownership.
RDAP and WHOIS accept hostnames or public IPs. URLs, paths, local/reserved addresses and unknown public suffixes are not accepted.

RDAP disclosure and service coverage vary. Missing fields remain missing. No DNS or website test, external link follow-up, WHOIS fallback, automatic retry or ownership/purchase conclusion is performed.

Requesting the registry response over TCP 43

WHOIS sends the displayed domain or public IP in plaintext over TCP 43 to the reviewed registry, or IANA and referred registries. A domain service-directory query sends its TLD to IANA. These services and the network path can observe the query and connection IP. Responses may contain contact data; they stay in memory, without logging or History.
View details for the registry response. WHOIS text does not provide standardized result status.
Plaintext TCP 43 uses the active network and its configured proxy route. Public-IP queries follow bounded IANA/RIR referrals. Networks or proxies may block TCP 43.

Registry text is not proof of ownership. Domain services come from reviewed IANA entries or the IANA TLD directory; public IPs use bounded IANA/RIR referrals. No retry or protocol fallback. Non-UTF-8 responses are unsupported.
No final regional registry record was identified. Available upstream responses remain in details.
